text.title: Guidance on the map
text.intro: A score field learned on the 2-D t-SNE of the 11,439 records pushes sampled points toward phase-separating (y = 1) or non-separating (y = 0) regions. First the methods (the score field, sampling along an iso-line, sampling inside a region), then four main results as interactive maps: hover a point for its start and end, the records next to it, the sequence change and the predictions. The other examples are collapsed at the end.

yc.title: From a (y, c) set
yc.intro: A (y, c) set is the group of records that share one label inside one condition cell. Chains start at the map positions of the start-label records (16 chains per record, 0.03 SD jitter) and are guided to the opposite label for 1,200 steps (Langevin, temperature 0.5, w = 4); the controls are no guidance and guidance to the same label. The GIF shows 24 chains (a frame every 10 steps, 60-step tail), left guided to y = 1 and right to y = 0; the black dots are the final positions and stay for 8 s. r is the log density ratio of the field, Δr its change from start to end; “within 0.10 SD” counts chains that end within 0.10 map SD of a record of the target label in the same cell; in the tables “none” is the control without guidance.

pts.title: From a map point to a sequence
pts.intro: A map point has no inverse in sequence space, so the decoder goes through the records around it. The anchor is the real sequence with the largest Gaussian weight among the neighbours of the point; the target is the ESMC-600M embedding (layer 18, z-scored, PCA to 64) of those neighbours. ESMC's masked language model proposes substitutions at random positions, added one at a time (an edit ladder: k substitutions after step k, sequences already in the library excluded). The answer is the step k* closest to the target; k* = 0 means the anchor itself is the best answer. D is the distance between the ESMC embedding (64-D, unit sphere) of a sequence and the target. The 12 points of a row are quantiles along the line of the exact samples of (region ∩ iso-line), 6 guided to y = 1 and 6 to y = 0.
limits: Many points return their anchor (k* = 0): the target embedding is then almost the anchor's own. The TDP-43 example is the one where most answers carry substitutions.
Positions are proposed at random and kept when they move the embedding toward the target; they are not chosen for function, and the decoded variants are not scored for phase separation here.

field.title: The score field
paras: A TorchEBM energy model E(u | y) is trained on the t-SNE coordinates u of the records only (conditional denoising score matching, 15% label dropout, Fourier features), with kernel width σ = 0.16 inside the data, rising smoothly to 0.50 outside. Its direction agrees with the analytic Gaussian-KDE score (cosine 0.994). The guidance direction is s(u | 1) − s(u | 0) = ∇ log p(u | 1) − ∇ log p(u | 0); guided sampling uses the classifier-free energy E_n + w (E_y − E_n).
facts: It describes the label layout of this map. With papers held out (checked on the first, σ = 0.12 field), the share of arrows pointing toward y = 1 is 0.469 (labels permuted: 0.42), so it does not predict labels for new papers.

Guidance works, within limits: guiding to y = 1 raises the share of samples that land in the y = 1 territory from 67% (no guidance) to about 75% (the records themselves: 77%), and weights above w = 2 add nothing. Guiding to y = 0 with w = 4 pushes 28% of the samples outside the data, so w ≤ 2 is the usable range.
The field has no condition c as input: it only knows where the records of each label sit.

figs.cap: Score toward y = 1 on the t-SNE plane (36 × 36 lattice, every arrow drawn). Boxes: six sub-spaces that hold both labels and where y depends on the conditions.
Energies E(u | y), the log density ratio r(u) = log p(u | 1) − log p(u | 0), and where guided samples land (400 samples per setting).

groups.title: From a (y, c) set
groups.intro: A (y, c) set is the group of records that share one label inside one condition cell. Chains start at the map positions of the start-label records (16 chains per record, 0.03 SD jitter) and are guided to the opposite label for 1,200 steps (Langevin, temperature 0.5, w = 4); the controls are no guidance and guidance to the same label. The GIF shows 24 chains (a frame every 10 steps, 60-step tail), left guided to y = 1 and right to y = 0; the black dots are the final positions and stay for 8 s. r is the log density ratio of the field, Δr its change from start to end; “within 0.10 SD” counts chains that end within 0.10 map SD of a record of the target label in the same cell; in the tables “none” is the control without guidance.
limits: Guided chains move the right way (50–100% of them toward the target label, against 6–88% without guidance), but they do not end next to records of the opposite label in the same cell more often than unguided chains (at most 8% within 0.10 SD).
Why: the field has no condition c as input, so “from this (y, c) set” only chooses where the chains start; the guidance itself is the global y field. Fixing c needs a model that takes c as input.

groups.title: Along an iso-line of one condition
groups.intro: An iso-line is a smoothed contour of one covariate (sequence length, NaCl, temperature, pH, concentration, crowder) over the map. Chains are sampled on the line, parameterised by arc length, with TorchEBM's Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: 10 leapfrog steps of 0.05 SD per proposal, Metropolis acceptance, temperature 0.5, w = 4, 400 proposals, 60 start points × 8 chains. A chain cannot leave the line and stays in the piece of the line it starts on (a line has several pieces). The GIF shows 60 chains, left guided to y = 1 and right to y = 0, 4 proposals per frame, the black dots are the final positions. Homogeneity is how uniform the covariate is near the line (lower is better); TV is the distance of the sampled distribution to the exact one on the line.

fig.cap: Samplers compared on two iso-lines (480 chains each, equal cost): TorchEBM Langevin and HMC with the line written as a thin tube, and the same samplers on the 1-D arc-length coordinate.

limits: On a line: 1-D arc-length HMC. Distance to the exact distribution (TV) 0.07 on NaCl 150 mM and 0.15 on 22 °C, against 0.28 and 0.52 for the earlier projected Langevin; 0% of the chains leave the line (11% on the NaCl line before).

Inside a region cut out by several constraints: exact sampling on the 160 × 160 energy grid. The region has disconnected pieces and MCMC leaks between them (distance to the exact distribution 0.20–0.66, against a sampling noise floor of 0.05–0.15). HMC is for showing the process.
Both ends of a line sit next to the same proteins (87–99% shared in the Langevin run), so y differences along a line come from other conditions or from the source paper, not from the sequence.

groups.rule: A line is shown when the covariate is more uniform near it than across the data (homogeneity < 1), it is at least 1 SD long, at least 10 records of each label lie within 0.12 SD of it, r changes sign along it and at least 5 papers lie near it. The last two conditions were added when the new lines were chosen.

iso.title: Sampling along an iso-line
steps: Each covariate (sequence length, NaCl, temperature, pH, concentration, crowder) is smoothed over the map with a Gaussian kernel (σ = 0.16 map SD) into a field g(u); the iso-line is the contour g(u) = g₀. A line is kept when the covariate is uniform near it (homogeneity < 1), it is at least 1 SD long, at least 10 records of each label lie within 0.12 SD of it, r changes sign along it and at least 5 papers lie near it.
The line is parameterised by arc length s. A line has several pieces; each piece is an interval of s.
On a piece, p(s) ∝ exp(−E_w(u(s)) / T) with the guided energy E_w = E_n + w (E_y − E_n) of the TorchEBM conditional energy (σ = 0.16), w = 4, T = 0.5, y = 1 or y = 0.

Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on s (TorchEBM): 10 leapfrog steps of 0.05 SD per proposal, Metropolis accept/reject, steep walls at the ends of a piece, 400 proposals; 60 start points equally spaced in arc length × 8 chains per direction. The chain cannot leave the line and stays on the piece where it starts.
TV distance to the exact distribution on the line, acceptance rate, median move along the line, share of chains that end off the data.
recommend: Distance to the exact distribution (TV) 0.07 on NaCl 150 mM and 0.15 on 22 °C, against 0.28 and 0.52 for the earlier projected Langevin; 0% of the chains leave the line (11% on the NaCl line before). Langevin on the same coordinate gets stuck; HMC moves 0.3–1.3 SD along the line.

fig.cap: Samplers compared on two iso-lines (NaCl 150 mM and 22 °C; 480 chains each, equal cost): TorchEBM Langevin and HMC with the line written as a thin tube, and the same samplers on the 1-D arc-length coordinate.

region.title: Sampling inside a region
steps: Several conditions at once: F = {u : |g_k(u) − g_k0| ≤ τ_k for every constraint k, the area is data-supported, and the local spread of the covariate is at most 0.8 of its global spread}. The example in the results, C3, is 22 ± 4 °C, pH 7.5 ± 0.35, NaCl 150 mM (log₁₀(1 + x) ± 0.25) and 10 µM (log₁₀ ± 0.3): 735 cells of the 160 × 160 grid in 11 separate pieces.
The same guided energy E_w (w = 4, T = 0.5), tabulated on the grid; the probability of a cell inside the region is ∝ exp(−E_w / T).

Draw cells at random with these probabilities and jitter uniformly inside the cell. The samples are independent, there is nothing to tune and nothing leaves the region. HMC is kept for showing the process (the GIFs).

The pieces are disconnected: Langevin or HMC with a wall leaks out of the region (up to 16% of the chains) or cannot change piece; their distance to the exact distribution is 0.20–0.66, while exact sampling is as close as two independent exact samples are to each other (0.05–0.15, the sampling-noise floor).

table.caption: Distance to the exact distribution (TV, guided to y = 1 / to y = 0; the sampling-noise floor is 0.05–0.15) on three regions: C1 = 22 °C and pH 7.5; C3 = C1 plus 150 mM NaCl and 10 µM; L1 = 400 aa and 150 mM NaCl. MCMC chains start at random points inside the region; “largest leak” is the largest share of chains that ended outside it.

rows.title: SARS-CoV-2 N region ∩ protein concentration 10 µM

results.intro: Four results, each an interactive map on the t-SNE of the records. Hover (or tap) a point for its start and end, the records next to it (protein, paper, label, conditions), the score field's estimate and, for the decoded points, the sequence change and the FINCHES prediction. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click to pin a point; the legend toggles the groups.

maps.title: Iso-line: NaCl = 150 mM
desc: Chains start on the NaCl = 150 mM iso-line (60 equally spaced starts × 8 chains) and are guided to y = 1 (purple) or y = 0 (cyan) by 1-D arc-length HMC (400 proposals, w = 4). The line is 5.3 SD long in 5 pieces, with 749 records near it from 26 papers and 19 proteins.
reading: Guided ends sit on stretches of higher r (to y = 1: median r +0.08) or lower r (to y = 0: median r −0.30).

The proteins next to the two kinds of ends largely coincide (74% shared), so a large part of the y difference along an iso-line is not a sequence effect: it comes from other conditions or from the source paper.
Sampler checks: TV to the exact distribution 0.07 / 0.06, acceptance 0.76 / 0.81.

maps.title: Region: 22 °C, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 10 µM
desc: 500 independent exact samples per direction inside the region where all four constraints hold (22 ± 4 °C, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 10 µM): 735 grid cells (2.9% of the grid) in 11 pieces, with 613 records inside (452 y = 1, 161 y = 0) from 40 papers and 54 proteins.
reading: Samples guided to y = 1 sit at high r (median +2.7), those guided to y = 0 near −0.2: the field separates the two inside the region.
There is no start or end: exact samples are independent. Hover a sample for the records next to it (the reference) and the field's estimate.
Decoding to sequences is shown for points on a line (the last result).

maps.title: (y, c) set: physiological cell

facts.desc: 22 °C, pH 7.5, 100–200 mM NaCl, no crowder, 10–32 µM (cross-paper)

desc: Chains start at the records of one label in the physiological cell (22 °C, pH 7.5, 100–200 mM NaCl, no crowder, 10–32 µM; 82 y = 1 and 77 y = 0 records, 88 sequences, 43 papers) and are guided to the other label for 1,200 steps (Langevin, T = 0.5, w = 4; 16 chains per record, 0.03 SD jitter).
reading: Guided ends move in r in the intended direction (median Δr +0.54 for y = 0 → 1, −1.02 for y = 1 → 0), but they end within 0.10 SD of a record of the target label no more often than unguided chains (8% against 10%, 8% against 13%).
The two labels interleave on the map (mean r of the two classes differs by 0.05) and the field has no condition c as input, so the cell only decides where the chains start.
Switch on “unguided control ends” to see where chains without guidance end.

maps.title: Map point → sequence: tau region ∩ 10 µM line
desc: Twelve points of the exact samples of (tau region ∩ 10 µM iso-line), 6 guided to y = 1 and 6 to y = 0, decoded to sequences through the records around them: an anchor sequence plus ESMC masked-language-model substitutions that move the ESMC embedding toward the target. Start = the closest record of the anchor, end = the map point and the answer.
reading: 8 of the 12 answers are the anchor itself (k* = 0); 4 carry 2–12 substitutions.

FINCHES, over all 15 decoded variants of the five map-point examples: median |Δε| (Mpipi, full length) 0.94 for the decoded answers against 0.40 for random substitutions at the same sites, and 53% become more attractive: no consistent direction.
Positions are proposed at random and kept when they move the embedding toward the target; they are not chosen for function.
